name: High-Protein Beef Burrito Bowls
intro_html: This is the bowl that quietly ends your takeout habit. One skillet of seasoned lean beef, fluffy rice, black beans, and sweet corn, portioned into a week of dinners that each land near {{protein}} grams of protein without wrecking the grocery budget. Cook it Sunday, eat like a champ through Friday.
ingredients_display: 93/7 Ground Beef (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 5 cups (840 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): about 1 3/4 cups shredded (8 oz bag) (196 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Rice, 3.5 cups dry jasmine: ~$0.86. Buy 1 (covers this batch with some left over).
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn, 5 cups: ~$1.19. Buy 2 cans: $1.22.
Reduced Fat Mozzarella, about 1 3/4 cups shredded (8 oz bag): ~$1.50. Buy 1 8oz bag: $1.74.
Pantry seasonings (taco seasoning): ~$0.81. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $32.09 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.29 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $36.58 across 14 servings, roughly $2.61 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $0.38 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $36.96. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: That is about ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) versus $10 or more for a single fast-casual burrito bowl. The ground beef is your whole cost, so catch it on sale and this drops even lower.
shop_smart: Buy the beef on sale and freeze it. Lean ground beef goes on sale constantly. When it does, grab several pounds and freeze in one-pound packs. One buy can cover a month of these bowls.
Rice and beans are the cheap muscle. A big bag of rice and canned beans by the case cost pennies per serving. Compare the price per ounce, not the sticker, to find the real deal.
Store brand seasoning wins. A store-brand taco or fajita packet is a fraction of the name brand, and you can mix your own from chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic, and onion powder for even less.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Cook the rice. Three and a half cups dry jasmine with water per the package, then set aside.
Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks. At 93/7 there is little to drain.
Add the taco seasoning, the tomato paste, and a splash of water. Stir until the beef is coated and glossy.
Drain and rinse the black beans and corn, then warm them through.
Combine the rice, beef, beans, and corn in your big pot and stir. Fold in the shredded mozzarella so it melts into the warm mix.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1. That is your total food weight. Divide it by 14, then scoop that exact amount into each container. Every bowl lands right at about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein.
upsell_html: High-protein dinners for about ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up as it cooks.
